title: Three Kinds of Brackets
statement:
You are given `t` strings made only of the characters `(`, `)`, `[`, `]`, `{`, `}`. A string is **balanced** if every opening bracket is closed by a bracket of the *same kind*, and brackets are closed in the reverse order they were opened (so `([)]` is not balanced, but `([])` is).

**Input.** First line: `t`. Then `t` lines, each a non-empty string.

**Output.** For each string print `YES` if it is balanced, otherwise `NO`.
constraints: 1 ≤ t, total length of all strings ≤ 3000 in this browser version

hints: Counting how many of each bracket kind occur is not enough; `([)]` has matching counts but is wrong.
When you see a closing bracket, which opening bracket must be the most recent unmatched one? Which structure gives you 'most recent' in O(1)?
Push every opening bracket. On a closing bracket the stack must be non-empty and its top must be the matching opener; pop it. At the end the stack must be empty.
editorial:
Scan left to right with a stack of unmatched opening brackets. An opening bracket is pushed. A closing bracket must match the **top** of the stack (the most recently opened, still-unclosed bracket); if the stack is empty or the top is a different kind, the string is invalid. After the scan the stack must be empty, otherwise some opener was never closed.

Each character is pushed and popped at most once, so a string of length `L` costs `O(L)`.
